Linking this to RCS-28134. Same legacy LPMS on nettrack, same origin us.apprissretail.com, same 524, and neither account was migrated. Luis already traced the mechanism there: CommandTimeout is falling back to 120 seconds against Cloudflare's 100-second cutoff.

One difference worth noting: Casey's fails on save, while this one fails on read, on SystemSelect and the Open Investigations summary. One of the pages also returned "The service is unavailable," which is IIS rather than a timeout, so the app pool may be recycling on top of the slow query.

Investigation summary. LPUser queries on the Tailored Brands database averaged 0.5 to 0.8 seconds through August 5 and jumped to an average of 57 seconds with a 120-second maximum starting August 6, with the first bad plan appearing at 17:35 UTC. Same query IDs, new execution plans. The good ones were compiled with cardinality estimator 140, while the bad ones were compiled with 160.

All 137 production databases are now on compatibility level 160. Three are affected out of the 39 currently running this query.

The 120-second ceiling is the application CommandTimeout, and Cloudflare cuts at 100 seconds, which produces the 524.

Shared with Matt K, pending Engineering direction.

Client ID 209.

Colton Neal confirmed on August 11 that timeouts and incident creation are resolved for the users he spoke with. Izenda reporting is still timing out.

Evidence from the customer on August 11:
Cloudflare error 524 at 2026-08-11 18:56:16 UTC
Ray ID a299728c9ee465e3
Host us.apprissretail.com
This is a timeout, not a Cloudflare block.

Feature flags validated by Kiran Vadday on August 10 directly against the tenant database, at Matt Kamminga's request:

Feature.Incident.EnableAdHocInitCaching, True
Feature.Incident.EnableAdHocPerRequestUserScope, True
Feature.Incident.EnableBlobAppendLogging, False, edited 2026-08-10 14:09:57 UTC

The two flags Jon Morgan re-enabled at 12:12 on August 10 are confirmed True on this tenant, so they do not explain the reporting timeout.

Ruled out: a missing deployment. Kiran confirmed on August 11 that once deployed all clients receive the same code, so the hotfix released for RCS-28084 is present here.

Open and unowned: the Izenda reporting timeout. Ray ID and owner request posted in Teams. Expected value for EnableBlobAppendLogging still unconfirmed.

Sign in is resolved and confirmed by the customer.

1. Correction

ENG-7168 shipped in Secure August 2026 Release 2/2, released 27 August. It did not resolve the reported symptom.

Feature.Incident.EnableScreenLabelCaching resolves to True on this tenant, so the fix is active and the customer still measures 30 to 40 seconds. The flag is not the gap. Screen label caching is not what is costing the time on this path.

Support carried the assumption that the August release closed this. It did not, and the customer measured it six days after the release.

2. Environment and steps to reproduce

Production. Tenant 209-tbi, Tailored Brands. Database sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-209-tbi-platform. Web role web-prd-wus2-arp-nettrack.

Tailored Brands (TBI), reported 2026-09-02

  1. Sign in to Secure as a Tailored Brands user.

  2. Navigate from Secure to Incident. The transition lands on SystemSelect.aspx.

  3. Time the transition from click to rendered page.

Expected: not documented. Support does not hold a target load time for this path and is not inventing one.

Actual: 30 to 40 seconds, measured by Colton Neal on 2026-09-02.

Customer measurements on 2026-08-12, before the release:

User

Measured

Mike DiTommaso

45 s

Sam Fuentes

45 s

Colton Neal

30 s

Colton Neal on 2026-09-02, after the release: 30 to 40 s.

No improvement is visible in the customer-side numbers across the release boundary.

3. Findings

Feature flags read in production on 2026-09-08

Read against [Secure].[ConfigurationItem] on sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-209-tbi-platform. Both columns were read because GetConfigurationItem reads Value while the Control Panel writes CustomerEditedValue, documented by Chris Rippingale on ENG-7168, 2026-08-12.

Name

True

True

False

False

Feature.Incident.EnableScreenLabelCaching

True

NULL

This answers a question raised on ENG-7168 and never picked up

Chris Rippingale, ENG-7168, 2026-08-14:

"ENG-6680's blob fix is not active in prod. Zero AppendBlobClient.AppendBlock in 24 h; the legacy triad is still running (Exists 64,624, Upload 39,694, DownloadContent 35,023). Either not deployed or the flag is not resolving True for these tenants. Needs someone with prod DB access to check."

Checked. On tenant 209 the flag resolves to False. That accounts for the blob fix being inactive here.

Support does not know the intended value for Feature.Incident.EnableBlobAppendLogging. It was recorded as False on this tenant on 2026-08-10 at 14:09:57 UTC and the expected value has been unconfirmed since 2026-08-11. Confirming it is item 2 below.

Two causes identified in the same Profiler pass were never raised as work

Chris Rippingale, ENG-7168, 2026-08-14, items 2 and 3:

"Sync Redis inside the response output filter. DevExpressProxyResponseFilter.Close() and HtmlRewriteFilter.Close() both call ConfigurationInfo.GetGlobalConfigurationValue("UrlSlug", platformID) → blocking RedisDatabase.StringGet. Response filters run at flush time, per chunk, on every response. The Profiler's only Blocking-category finding, at 123,243 ms."

"Izenda pumps a WinForms message loop inside w3wp. AsyncDataSetFiller.FillDataSet waits on its async DB fill via System.Windows.Forms.Application.ThreadContext.RunMessageLoop. Highest-scoring prod finding."

Neither carries a ticket. Both were flagged as out of scope for ENG-7168 and nothing picked them up.

Chris also stated the limit of what ENG-7168 could recover, on 2026-08-14:

"How much of the unaccounted wall clock this PR recovers is not established, and item 2 above says at least some of it sits elsewhere. Expect partial improvement."

The customer measurement is consistent with that statement.

Tenant 209 was named in the ENG-7168 analysis

Chris Rippingale, ENG-7168, 2026-08-14:

"AdHoc tenants 209 (p50 78.8 s) and 041 (p50 10.2 s) are worse per-request than tenant 300, which reportedly has the AdHoc caching flags off. Suggests their flags are not actually applied, or a separate tenant-specific problem."

The AdHoc flags on 209 are applied. Both resolve to True. The first branch of that hypothesis is closed. The second branch, a tenant-specific problem on 209, is open and untested.

4. Troubleshooting performed, and the limits of support access

  1. Read all four Incident feature flags in production against the tenant database on 2026-09-08. Both Value and CustomerEditedValue columns, with the effective value computed the same way the application computes it.

  2. Confirmed ENG-7168 fixVersion and release date in Jira. Secure August 2026 Release 2/2, released 2026-08-27.

  3. Compared customer-reported timings across the release boundary, 2026-08-12 against 2026-09-02.

  4. Reviewed the ENG-7168 comment history for scope statements and out-of-scope findings.

AI use declared. Claude was used to consolidate the ticket history, cross-read ENG-7168 and ENG-6680, and draft this note. Every quotation above is copied from the cited Jira comment. The flag values were produced by Juan Martinez running the query in production, not by the model.

Conversations outside this ticket. Viraj Kansara posted a Teams link on 2026-08-18 to Retail Ops, AALPS Issues channel. J.R. Teagle exchanged email with Mike DiTommaso on 2026-08-16 and pasted both sides into this ticket. No other calls or channels.

What support cannot see. Application Insights Profiler traces for web-prd-wus2-arp-nettrack scoped to tenant 209 across the release boundary. Support cannot attribute the remaining wall clock without them.

5. Ruled out. Do not repeat

Hypothesis

Refutation

The ENG-7168 fix never reached this tenant

EnableScreenLabelCaching resolves to True in production, read 2026-09-08

The AdHoc caching flags are off on 209

Both resolve to True, read 2026-09-08

A flag toggled in Control Panel is invisible to the app here

CustomerEditedValue was read alongside Value. No divergence on the three flags that carry both

Sign-in and incident save are still failing

Customer confirmed both resolved on 2026-09-02

6. Still open

  1. Confirm what carries the remaining 30 to 40 seconds on the Secure to Incident transition for tenant 209, now that screen label caching is active and has not moved the customer-side number. SystemSelect.aspx is the landing page for this path.

  2. Confirm the intended value of Feature.Incident.EnableBlobAppendLogging. It is False on tenant 209 and has been unconfirmed since 2026-08-11. If the intended value is True, say so and this becomes a config change rather than engineering work.

  3. Decide whether the sync Redis call in DevExpressProxyResponseFilter.Close() and HtmlRewriteFilter.Close() gets its own ticket. It was the only Blocking-category Profiler finding at 123,243 ms and it runs per chunk on every response.

  4. Decide whether the Izenda WinForms message loop in AsyncDataSetFiller.FillDataSet gets its own ticket. It was the highest-scoring production Profiler finding and it matches the customer's reporting complaints on this ticket.

Related: ENG-7168, ENG-6680, RCS-28134, RCS-27941.
